newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila asks Netherlands to allow rebel to stay.
newsitem.headline: Manila asks Netherlands to allow rebel to stay.

text.p: Manila has asked The Hague to allow leftist Philippine rebel leader Jose Maria Sison to extend his stay while Manila officials and the rebels hold peace talks in the Dutch city of Utrecht, the government said on Tuesday.
Sison has refused Manila's invitation to return from the Netherlands and rebel sources said his reluctance was based on fears for his safety in his home country.

Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon told reporters that if Sison were allowed to stay in the Netherlands, the self-exiled founder of the Philippine Communist Party could come to the Philippines without the pressure of having to stay.
The Dutch government last year rejected Sison's request for asylum and told him to leave. Sison is appealing against the decision.
Utrecht is hosting peace talks between Manila and the communist-led National Democratic Front (NDF) aimed at ending a 28-year Marxist insurgency.
The Philippines has said it hopes to reach a peace deal with the NDF by the end of June.
More than 40,000 people have died in the insurgency that began in 1969.
